therapeutic_hypothesis.claimed_target: reactive oxygen species / mitochondrial electron transport chain
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Elderly subjects in three cognitive groups: Alzheimer's disease (AD), mild cognitive impairment (MC), and cognitively normal elderly (CNE)
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change in brain glucose metabolism measured by 18FDG-PET from baseline to week 4

results.effect_size: Median SUVBSA2 changes ranged from -8.56 to +4.60 across brain regions; no statistically significant difference between EGb761 and placebo reported
biomarker_changes: 18FDG-PET SUVBSA2 median changes were small and overlapping between EGb761 and placebo across all brain regions at 4 weeks
At 18 months open-phase, median SUVBSA2 changes were near zero across all brain regions in both CNE and MC groups
MRI voxel-based morphometry showed variable changes in brain region volumes with wide confidence intervals
subgroup_findings: 1 MC subject converted to Alzheimer's dementia by DSM-IV and NINCDS-ADRDA criteria at month 9; 0 conversions at month 18
Cognitive test scores (MMSE, CDR, GDS, FCSRT, TMT, WAIS, MEM III) showed median changes near zero in both CNE and MC groups at months 9 and 18
No deaths due to TEAEs in any phase
safety_signals: 1 serious AE (transient ischaemic attack) in EGb761 double-blind phase (1/23)
6 serious AEs in EGb761 open phase (atrial fibrillation, cholelithiasis, sciatica, spinal cord compression, subclavian artery stenosis, lung neoplasm; each 1/41)
4 TEAEs leading to withdrawal in open phase; 1 in double-blind EGb761; 2 in placebo

context.indication: Alzheimer's disease and cognitive impairment (mild cognitive impairment and cognitively normal elderly)
context.duration: 4 weeks double-blind phase for AD; 18 months for MC and CNE groups
